title: Contribution Of Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Imaging In The Study Of Diabetic Cardiomyopathy
brief_summary: Diagnosis of diabetic cardiomyopathy is then retained, supposing a change in the coronary microcirculation linked to an endothelial dysfunction. Abnormalities of the myocardial metabolism is frequently associated. It is regrettably about a hypothesis difficult to verify with current medical techniques.This deficiency being not only harmful to the diagnosis, but also to the assessment of the efficiency of the medical treatment on the myocardial metabolism and the endothelial function. Techniques of nuclear magnetic resonance offer interesting perspectives.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* more than 18 years old
* patient type 2 diabetes affects taken care more than 5 years to Timone Hospital
* patient with a diabetic cardiomyopathy
* informed and consented

Exclusion Criteria:

* less than 18 years
* Pregnant woman
* patient type 1 diabetes affects
* patient presents a cardiomyopathy mixed (no diabetic)
* patients presents an arrhythmia ventriculaire or above - ventriculaire
* Unstable hémodynamique patients
